theme.name: National skills shortages and productivity
theme.claim: The manifesto commitment to three million apprenticeships is driven by the need to address national skill shortages and stimulate economic growth and productivity.

text.line: The Government’s manifesto commitment to achieve three million apprenticeship starts by 2020 is driven by an ambition to address our nation’s skill shortages and stimulate economic growth.

theme.name: Public sector apprenticeship gap
theme.claim: The public sector lags behind the private sector in apprenticeship uptake and has been asked to achieve a greater proportion of growth to close this gap.

text.line: The public sector has been asked to achieve a greater proportion of apprenticeship growth to bring us in line with the private sector where an estimated three-quarters of apprentices work.

theme.name: Civil Service diversity and inclusivity shortfall
theme.claim: Despite being the most diverse it has ever been, the Civil Service still lacks true representation and inclusivity, limiting social mobility.

text.line: The Workforce Plan also sets an ambition for the Civil Service to be the most inclusive employer in the UK.
Traditionally, the public sector has struggled to get right the diversity of its workforces and applicant pools.
Whilst the Civil Service is the most diverse it has ever been, we still have more to do to ensure true representation and inclusivity across the organisation.

theme.name: Disability employment gap
theme.claim: Disabled groups, such as those with autism, face a significant employment challenge that apprenticeships and wider policy must address.

text.line: This is a significant challenge for some disabled groups, with only 15% of people who have autism currently in full time employment.
We have more progress to make in changing the traditional view of apprenticeships, to ensure that equity of opportunity is achieved.
